title: Live meeting and speech classification
what: Tag sentences while they are still being spoken.

shape.state: one transcribed sentence, with the speaker
shape.question: choice over your categories, plus a noul for whether it is an action
shape.answer: one tag per sentence, accumulating into live notes

use: Stream the audio through speech to text, and send each finished sentence as its own call, because a sentence is short and the answer comes back before the next one lands. Sentences are sorted into decisions, action items, risks and questions, which is a meeting record written as it happens. The video's example on the same shape scores a debate as it is spoken, one sentence at a time.

code.label: one finished sentence, one tag

prompts.question: kind=choice:How should Priya's sentence be filed in the minutes?|decision:A choice the room committed to,action:Something one named person will do,risk:A problem or dependency raised,question:Something still unanswered

title: Zero LLM retrieval engine
what: Answer narrow questions from a fixed corpus with no text generation at all.

shape.question: choice over indexed topic units, plus a noul for whether the corpus covers it
shape.answer: the matching item and its timestamp; no prose

use: Turn the transcripts you already have into topic units with a short description each, then match the question against them. The visitor gets the actual answer slot, a lesson number or a video timestamp, which is more useful than a paragraph about it and costs nothing to generate. The corpus has to be genuinely finite for this to work, and the no-match case must be allowed to come back empty.

code.label: index once, answer from the list

title: Dynamic UI icon selection
what: Pick the picture that matches what the user just typed.

shape.question: choice over icon keys in your set

use: Map a fixed icon set to descriptive keys and choose between them as the field changes. A habit tracker draws the water glass when someone types drink more water; a mood log draws the face that matches the entry. The alternative is a keyword matcher that misses and an LLM call that costs far more for the same answer.

code.label: text in, icon key out

title: Just in time page assembly
what: Choose the parts a visitor needs and build the page from them.

shape.state: the visitor's signals, written as facts
shape.question: one choice per slot in the layout
shape.answer: which module fills each slot; your code renders them

use: Build a library of finished components, forms, buttons, sign-up boxes, headings and type presets, and let Jev choose which one fills each slot for this visitor. Nothing is generated at request time, so the page costs a normal page load: the model is choosing between things you already built, and every branch stays reviewable in code. Ask one question per slot, and keep a default for every slot.

code.label: one question per slot, parts already built

title: Workflow use case auditing
what: Find the steps in your own work that should have been a decision, not a model call.

shape.state: one step from a log or a process document
shape.question: choice for the shape of the step, a noul for whether a decision model fits
shape.answer: a list of candidate steps, sorted by how well they fit

use: Walk your own logs or process notes and ask, of each step, whether a typed decision would have done the job. The answer space is closed: either a decision fits, or the step needs writing, or it is a count and belongs in code. The same audit runs over a public catalogue of use cases when you are looking for ideas rather than for your own work.

code.label: label each step, sort in code
